analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of docs/developer/test.md (lines 1751-2705). Only documentation changed, with no executable code, config, workflow or permission changes in the supplied text. The text describes test procedures for the prompt-contract sidecar (Go/Rust pairing, preload selection, capacity), connected-cache batching, Provider CI lanes, coverage, and SSD cache authentication tests.

Security-relevant observations:
- The documented SSD tests (`tamperFailsClosed` requiring `SSDBlockStoreError.authenticationFailed`, the donation-gate tests, in-memory KEK) are consistent with T-041's mitigations (DBK3 AES-GCM AAD authentication, HMAC lookup tags, per-donation gate). The docs state these tests do not exercise a hardware-backed key or persistent-Keychain, which is a coverage limitation rather than a regression.
- The docs give no instruction to use production credentials, endpoints or signing. They explicitly forbid replacing fixture URLs or tokens with production ones.
- The connected-cache B2 text says its test trust/billing and ephemeral cache keys are not production attestation, so it does not overclaim TB-009, TB-011 or App Attest.
- Test-fixture env vars (DARKBLOOM_TEST_PROMPT_SIDECAR*, DARKBLOOM_PLANNING_TEST_UDS_PARENT) are test-only and require hash-bound binaries and a private UDS parent. No new runtime attack surface is introduced.
- No threat-model claim is contradicted or invalidated.

No cross-file interactions are changed. Later passes need only confirm that no code in the same PR relaxes the behaviors these docs describe (SSD tamper authentication, TTL, App Attest gating). The excerpt I received did not include any such code.
